# `respawn-rules` content schema

<!-- Generated by pnpm content:docs from the "respawn-rules" schema in src/content/registry.ts; do not edit. -->

One JSON file per entry in `src/content/data/respawn-rules/`. Fields marked "required" must be present;
every other field takes the default shown when omitted ("—" = stays absent).

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `id` | `"respawn-rules"` | required | Always "respawn-rules": there is one rule table. |
| `notes` | string | required | What the table covers and why. |
| `deathBeatSeconds` | number 0–10 | required | Seconds of sim time from the player’s death to the death screen. |
| `rules` | list of object | required | The rules, in any order. |
| `rules[].id` | id | required | Unique among the rules; breaks priority ties (lowest id wins). |
| `rules[].notes` | string | — | Why the rule exists. |
| `rules[].region` | ref → scene | required | The scene the player dies in for this rule to apply. |
| `rules[].priority` | integer | `0` | Of every matching rule the highest priority wins. |
| `rules[].conditions` | `condition` | — | A world-fact condition that must hold (docs/design/conditions.md); omit: always. |
| `rules[].destination` | object | required | Where the player comes back: the wake-in-place spot, or the start when a reload finds no save. |
| `rules[].destination.scene` | ref → scene | required | The scene of the spawn point. |
| `rules[].destination.spawn` | id | required | A spawn id that scene places. |
| `rules[].mode` | `"reload"` \| `"wake-in-place"` | required | reload: the death screen and Load last save; wake-in-place: wake at the destination. |
| `rules[].factsToSet` | list of object | `[]` | Facts written when the rule is chosen. |
| `rules[].factsToSet[].fact` | string | required | A declared fact. |
| `rules[].factsToSet[].value` | boolean or integer or string | required | A bool, a whole number or a string, fitting the fact type. |

## `condition`

A condition over world facts: one of fact, count, all, any, not (docs/design/conditions.md).

A `condition` is exactly one of these objects:

### 1. Tests one fact, with at most one operator.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `fact` | string | required | Fact key to test. Alone: the (bool) fact is true. With one operator: that comparison holds. |
| `eq` | boolean or integer or string | — | The fact equals this value. |
| `neq` | boolean or integer or string | — | The fact does not equal this value (unset counts as unequal). |
| `gt` | integer | — | The (int or tick) fact is greater than this. |
| `gte` | integer | — | The (int or tick) fact is at least this. |
| `lt` | integer | — | The (int or tick) fact is less than this. |
| `lte` | integer | — | The (int or tick) fact is at most this. |
| `has` | boolean | — | true: the fact holds a value (set, or declared with a non-null default); false: none. |

### 2. Counts true entity facts matching a pattern, compared with exactly one operator.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `count` | string | required | Entity facts to count: `entity:<level>/*.<fact>` (one level) or `entity:*/*.<fact>` (every level). Counts those holding true. |
| `eq` | integer | — | The count equals this. |
| `neq` | integer | — | The count does not equal this. |
| `gt` | integer | — | The count is greater than this. |
| `gte` | integer | — | The count is at least this. |
| `lt` | integer | — | The count is less than this. |
| `lte` | integer | — | The count is at most this. |

### 3. True when every condition in the list holds.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `all` | list of `condition` (at least 1) | required | Every condition holds. |

### 4. True when at least one condition in the list holds.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `any` | list of `condition` (at least 1) | required | At least one holds. |

### 5. True when the condition does not hold.

| Field | Type | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `not` | `condition` | required | The condition that must not hold. |
